key_insight: Centered finite-volume transport with explicit pressure relaxation nearly preserves kinetic energy in weakly compressible single- and two-phase flows, while harmonic face densities help maintain positive phase masses.
engineering_relevance: The method supports low-dissipation multiphase turbulence simulation and offers a foundation for future GPU-based large-eddy simulation with adaptive mesh refinement.
method: Couple kinetic-energy-preserving centered advection with conservative diffuse-interface regularization.
Use harmonic face densities to connect phase-volume and phase-mass transport.
Apply pressure-increment relaxation with compatible cell and face operators on structured collocated grids.
evidence_signal: In inviscid turbulence on 128³ cells at t*=8, relative kinetic-energy changes stayed below 1.2×10⁻⁷ in magnitude for single-phase and density-ratio-1000 two-phase cases; matched upwind runs retained only 3.60% and 30.72% of initial energy, respectively.
watch_item: Phase-mass positivity and the additional-pressure-iteration energy estimate are conditional; centered transport relies on a prescribed subgrid-scale stress for principal dissipation.
paper_title: A centered finite-volume method with explicit pressure relaxation for weakly compressible single- and two-phase flows
